Alicia — thanks for the clear asks. I reviewed the spreadsheet and drafted a MAP skeleton attached. Quick notes inline:

- Dedicated vs Private lead time: Dedicated (hosted, reserved GPUs) typical procurement-to-availability 8–12 weeks; Private (VPC + on-prem options) 12–20 weeks depending on on-prem approvals and KMS/HSM integration.
- Hedging: we recommend a staged reserve (20–40% tranche) to cover initial traffic while private infra is provisioned — details in the draft.
- Sizing: need confirmation on 95th-percentile QPS and model choice (we assumed a 13B-chat baseline for the draft). Two scenarios included: conservative (2x headroom) and aggressive (4x headroom).
- Acceptance: defined minimal SLOs (p95 latency, error budget), successful load test at 80% projected peak, and security review completion (SOC2 evidence).

Can you confirm: 95th pctl QPS in the sheet (row 7) is ~1.2k? Also, when does Procurement want the commitment window to begin (month)?

Regards,

Subject: RE: MAP kickoff — capacity & lead times (internal sizing notes)

Looping in sizing & pricing recommendations for Horizon. Summary:

- Baseline assumption: 13B chat model (int8 quantized) at 1.2k QPS 95th with average seq 384 tokens.
- Conservative pool: 8x A100-80GB equiv (target throughput for steady 1.2k QPS with 2x headroom).
- Aggressive pool: 16x A100-80GB equiv (4x headroom for bursty traffic, multi-region failover).
- Lead times: reseller-sourced Dedicated capacity ~8–12 weeks for tranche 1; Private on-prem baseline 14–20 weeks including KMS and compliance checks.
- Hedging playbook: propose a two-tranche reserve: tranche A (immediate, 25% capacity) to be provisioned on commit; tranche B (remaining) staged over the subsequent 8 weeks. This minimizes cost while mitigating supply lead-time risk.

Attachments: a sizing workbook and a short note on acceptance gating (load test protocol, perf benchmarks). Ben — can you pull estimated list pricing for both pools and a discounted tranche schedule we can put in the MAP? Marissa — adding you for rollout sequencing and SLA notes.

Karthik
Director, Capacity & Performance, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: gpu_sizing_scenarios.xlsx (xlsx)]

Subject: MAP: Horizon Labs — Finalized capacity hedging & acceptance plan (next steps)

Team — thanks for the inputs. Attached is the MAP we will present to Procurement; below is the condensed decision & milestone timeline.

Mutual Action Plan (high level):
1) Sign MAP & agreement on tranche schedule — target by 2026-06-25. (Owner: Horizon / Procurement)
2) Tranche A provisioned (25% capacity) — upon contract activation (target 2026-09-01). (Owner: Redwood Ops)
3) Tranche B staged provisioning (remaining capacity) — over 8 weeks from tranche A. (Owner: Redwood Ops)
4) Acceptance gating: successful load test at 80% projected peak, documented p95 latency < 250ms, error rate < 1%, SOC2 evidence collected. (Owner: Horizon + Redwood)
5) Fallback: if Private/VPC lead time slips beyond 12 weeks, Redwood will maintain a hot-warm failover with Dedicated hosted capacity for up to 12 weeks at pre-agreed rates.

Action items (next 30 days):
- Horizon: confirm 95th percentile QPS and final preferred model by 2026-06-01.
- Redwood: provide tranche pricing (Ben) and final MAP PDF (soojin) by 2026-06-10.
- Procurement: target internal review 2026-07-01; contract signature window 2026-07-15–2026-08-01.

Attachments: MAP-Final-Horizon-20260525.pdf (contains pricing appendix, acceptance checklist, and rollout calendar).
